lede: The biggest item this week is Town Council's first reading on Tuesday of Land Use Code amendments tied to Colorado's wildfire resilience requirements — real changes to how buildings get built in a box canyon that knows fire risk firsthand. Council will also hold a second work session on the Telluride Energy initiative, and the Housing Authority meets the same day to seat its new Resident Advisory Committee from a pool of fifteen tenant applicants. Across town, the week fills out with the Liquor Licensing Authority handling fourteen summer event permits, the BOCC weighing in on high-country road access with the Forest Service, and Ouray County's Planning Commission quietly working through land-use definitions that shape everything downstream.
